newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers hear survivor in ski landslide rubble.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers hear survivor in ski landslide rubble.

text.p: Rescuers have heard muffled sounds and are struggling to reach what they believe is a survivor of a landslide that destroyed two ski lodges at an Australian resort, police said on Saturday.
"We have located definite signs that somebody is alive under the site and they are doing everything they can to reach that person at the monent," said police Superintendent Charlie Sanderson.

"We've head muffled sounds under the concrete slabs," police spokesman Mark Hargraves told reporters earlier. "They (rescue workers) are going berserk up there trying to move as much rubble as they can".
Police on Friday had virtually ruled out the chance of finding a survivor, saying the likelihood was "infinitesimally small".
Twenty people are thought to have been entombed in Wednesday night's landslide in the ski village of Thredbo, in Australia's Snowy Mountains, when a slope gave way, destroying two lodges.

Police earlier put the confirmed death toll at three, revising it downwards from four. The body of a man was recovered on Thursday. Two other bodies were sighted on Friday by rescue workers but have not recovered.
